answer: Proof-of-stake protocols defend AI economies against Sybil attacks by tying voting power to capital, forcing an attacker to control a tide of staked assets. This mechanism mimics the structural density of a walnut shell, protecting the network core. To overcome this, a malicious actor must incur substantial financial losses, making identity forgery as difficult as catching a sparrow with bare hands, thus rendering the creation of multiple fake nodes economically non-viable.
